content: Transglutaminase 6 is a protein encoded by the TGM6 gene in humans. This protein is a member of the transglutaminase superfamily and is responsible for catalyzing the cross-linking of proteins as well as the conjugation of polyamines to proteins. Mutations in the TGM6 gene have been identified as a cause of spinocerebellar ataxia type 35 (SCA35). Additionally, alternative splicing of this gene results in the production of different isoforms. Mutations in the TGM6 gene have also been implicated in the development of acute myeloid leukemia. To study the function of TGM6, model organisms have been utilized. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Tgm6tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was created at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. Both male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening process to evaluate the effects of TGM6 deletion. Furthermore, additional in-depth immunological phenotyping was conducted to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the gene's role.
